title: Single-object homology normalization commutes with shift
statement: Let C be an abelian category with a chosen derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], Y : C and n : ℤ. Write H₀ for H^0 on D⁺(C), and χ_i : H^i(single_i Y) ≅ Y for singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso i. Define d : H^n(single_n Y) ≅ H^0(single_0 Y) by applying H^n to the inverse singleFunctors.shiftIso (-n) n 0, then applying H₀.shiftIso (-n) n 0. Then d.hom followed by χ_0.hom equals χ_n.hom. This concerns a single object in one abelian category, with no additive functor, enough-injectives assumption, cycles of a mapped complex, or derived unit.

proof.text: Use the fully faithful inclusion of D⁺(C) to identify its lifted single-functor shift with the derived single-functor shift. Use the induced shift-sequence comparison of quotient homology to transport to cochain complexes; naturality cancels the quotient homology comparison maps in inverse pairs.

For the literal single complex, the inverse shift map followed by the homology shift is induced by a morphism of short complexes whose middle component is the identity on Y. The outer terms are zero, so their shift signs make no contribution. Compose with the epimorphic homology projection. Naturality of homologyπ and cyclesMap_i identifies both paths with iCycles followed by singleObjXSelf.hom. Cancel the projection. For n=0 the shift unit comparisons cancel; for Y zero the same natural maps apply.
